form: vocative singular feminine (with elision of final -ε before following vowel)
meaning: sitting on an embroidered throne; with intricate throne; richly-throned
etymology: Compound of ποικίλος (variegated, embroidered, intricate) + θρόνος (throne, chair), likely Sapphic coinage or rare archaic epithet.
in_context: Functions as a vocative epithet directly addressing Aphrodite, emphasizing the goddess's regal splendor and the ornate craftsmanship of her divine seat in this invocation from Sappho Fragment 1.
